featured.title: If you can see it…you can be it – the power of mentorship
featured.subtitle: Natasha Granholm, CPA on LinkedIn

slides.title: If you can see it…you can be it – the power of mentorship
slides.subtitle: Natasha Granholm, CPA on LinkedIn
slides.description: How do we help build a better future? It’s a question many leaders ask themselves every day. Last night, I heard accomplished women from business, government and non-profits answer this question at Fortune’s Most Powerful Women dinner in Washington, D.C. After listening to these exceptional women leaders, some of whom are participants in the Fortune/U.S. State Department Global Women’s Mentoring Partnership, and sharing my own story, one thing was clear—mentorship is key to building a better future together. Growing up, I never imagined taking part in such a distinguished event. I was raised in a suburb of Chicago, predominantly by my grandmother and mother. Neither of them graduated from high school but, from as early as I can remember, they stressed the importance of education and were convinced it would lead to a better life. Yet as the first woman in my family to graduate from college, I found it difficult to envision a path that would help me achieve my goals. I had the education but no playbook for what comes next. To get to where I am today, I had to learn to adapt to, and excel in, many different environments, which would not have been possible without the many mentors who guided me along the way. It may seem odd, but it was actually a rejection early in my career that changed my way of thinking about what I was capable of achieving. Wanting a change, I applied for a job with a new company—a position I now realize would likely have limited my career advancement. Certain I had nailed the interview, I was surprised when the VP of the department asked to meet with me and then told me he wasn’t going to offer me the job. He told me his company didn’t have the opportunities I would need to reach my full potential. He advised me to stay put. The job I had, he believed, would challenge me more than making a move and could lead to significant opportunities in the future. He was right. Not long afterwards I traveled from Chicago, where I had always lived, to Washington D.C. to do a two-year of “tour of duty” with PwC. In Washington, I had the good fortune to meet and be mentored by African American executives in the firm, and it was a life-changing experience. I realized that until that point I hadn’t seen many people of color or women in high-level positions. After doing so, I was able to visualize a new career path and define more ambitious goals for myself. I adopted a mantra that I often share with the young people I mentor and my colleagues: If you can see it, you can be it. I had to see what was possible before I could become the professional that I am today. I realize it takes more to succeed than being able to imagine the end goal—it takes the willingness to jump into the unknown, change direction and accept new challenges. Six years ago, my mentors at PwC encouraged me to transition into the financial services sector at a time when I felt secure and successful in my role in our Deals Practice. It was a big move for me, but I had learned—thanks to my mentors over the years—not to limit my options and to trust myself. It was the smartest move I could have made, and I have never looked back. Looking ahead, I am optimistic about seeing more women and people of color in positions of leadership in every sector and industry. I want to open doors for my young colleagues and I want my twin daughters and my son to dream big and set their sights high. I look forward to hearing that a mentee in the audience at Fortune’s Most Powerful Women event this week has launched a successful start-up or been named CEO of a global company. Her leadership can inspire others who will see her and can strive to set their sights higher.

slides.title: Helping High School Teachers Better Understand the Accounting Profession is Key to Increasing the Number of Future CPAs
slides.subtitle: Natasha Granholm, CPA on LinkedIn
slides.description: When people would ask me what I wanted to be when I grew up, my answer was never “an accountant” or “a tax specialist.” This ambition was something that developed over time through life experiences and relationships made on my educational path. Like many young people in America, I was raised in a working class family and didn’t have substantive exposure to, or an understanding of, financial literacy, or a clear view of what an accountant actually does. Today, there are countless students who, like me, grew up with limited awareness of the importance of financial capabilities and the benefits of pursuing a career in accounting or financial services. A recent PwC survey found that only 12 percent of teachers address personal finance in their lessons, even though 92 percent believe financial education should be taught in schools.[1] That’s why PwC launched the Earn Your Future (EYF) initiative, a five-year, $190 million commitment focused on helping students develop critical financial capabilities. As part of the EYF initiative, I recently spoke to 80 high school educators at the PwC and Knowledge@Wharton High School (KWHS) seminar. This program is helping to create a better understanding of financial capabilities and accounting-related professions among teachers, so they can seamlessly integrate this knowledge into their classrooms across the country. And it’s working—after attending the PwC-KWHS seminar, more than 90 percent of surveyed educators felt confident or very confident teaching financial literacy and business responsibility. As I explained to the educators at the PwC and KWHS seminar, building financial capabilities among young people not only empowers them with life skills, but also with potential career skills. Further, I explained that it was imperative they walk away with an understanding of what a modern day accountant does, so that they can take this vision back to the classroom and incorporate it into their studies. Although bookkeeping and tax return preparation is still part of the role of an accountant – there is so much more to the profession! We can see the acute impact of this lack of exposure and experience to financial capability in the number of students pursuing careers in financial services sectors. In fact, according to a recent university study on the accounting field, the percentage of African Americans enrolled in bachelor’s degree accounting programs declined from about 11 percent in 2001–2002 to 7.2 percent in 2011–2012.[2] Those of us in accounting and financial services have to ask ourselves: Why aren’t students, and more specifically, students from diverse backgrounds, pursuing careers in our industry? According to the Howard University study, “young people, including underrepresented minorities, hold the profession in relatively low regard,” and reportedly don’t appreciate the career opportunities offered by the profession. Advocates for the industry are also few and far between—the study found that accounting isn’t a well-respected profession among parents and educators, who are among a student’s most trusted resources for information and support. What students, teachers and parents may not recognize however, is that accounting offers a variety of job opportunities and well-compensated positions. Also, contrary to popular belief, accountants and auditors are no longer merely “numbers people,” as the use of technology is opening doors for students with other critical STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Math) skills. While programs like EYF are helping to reverse this trend, another way to change the perceptions about careers in finance is to expand internship, scholarship and mentorship programs that can serve to expose students to the profession through direct and positive experiences. Opportunities like these were something that helped me and I think it can help countless others. Over the past four years, I’ve worked to build a recruiting pipeline for students from my alma mater, Robert Morris University, and other Chicago-based universities. Initiatives like these and EYF are critical to increasing the number of students in accounting and financial services, I think it’s just as important to expose students to real-life examples of success. I encourage all leaders in the accounting and financial service industries, regardless of gender, race or background, to share their story. My hope is that collectively, we can guide students not only towards financial health, but a potential financial career. [1] https://www.pwc.com/us/en/about-us/corporate-responsibility/assets/pwc-financial-education-report.pdf [2] http://howardcae.org/pipeline_2014.pdf

slides.title: Strengthening the Strategy around Diversity
slides.subtitle: Natasha Granholm, CPA on LinkedIn
slides.description: This week, I had the honor of engaging in an essential dialogue centered on how optimistic people feel about the state of diversity and inclusion. Disappointingly, not one person in the audience indicated they were optimistic but what we all agreed on is that NOW is the time to double down on our diversity and inclusion efforts. It’s not just the right thing to do, it’s the right thing to do for business. Too often we say we care about diversity and we cite to the millions our companies spend on diversity programs. As executives, entrepreneurs and innovators, we must individually rise to the challenge each and every day to make a collective impact. Within PwC, we’re continuing to make strides toward achieving even greater diversity, both for our firm and our industry, through initiatives such as Aspire to lead, a global series on leadership and gender equality, and our Start internship, which is designed to help college students develop foundational skills for the business world. But it doesn’t stop there. On the heels of tragic incidents in the news during a volatile summer, our US Chairman, Tim Ryan, was struck by the depth and immediacy of how these situations affected our people--and how much they wanted to connect with others to process what was unfolding. He was moved to organize candid conversations across the country -- to have a difficult, but necessary dialogue about race in the workplace. It was a bold first move for someone who, at the time, had been in his position less than 30 days. This was our leader rising to the challenge, but it was also about PwC, as a diverse organization, coming together as one. From this, our efforts have multiplied. Partners across the US have been actively engaging in conversations with their teams about the state of our nation and the too often tragic events that have a profound impact on all of us. We are focused on ensuring each member within our organization is understood in a more meaningful way and that it is understood that PwC is a place where we value all people. At Fortune’s Most Powerful Women Next Gen Summit, this was the focus of my conversation, as it’s been at the forefront of business and culture a great deal this year. Specifically, I discussed how to make businesses stronger through diversity. The straightforward answer lies in each of us holding ourselves accountable by answering the tough questions and acting on what we find. As a community, we asked ourselves: Do we expand beyond the “usual suspects” to collaborate on work assignments? Are we mentoring staff with experiences different than our own? Are we helping to seek out talent with diverse perspectives – and not just diverse racial or ethnic backgrounds? Are we aware of any unconscious biases? These are the conversations we need to continue to have and the questions we need to continue to ask ourselves. Diversity is not just about race or ethnicity, it’s also about ideas and experiences, considered judgment and perspective. This is the diversity that makes a business stronger, which may make all of us stronger. Following my session, I am optimistic about the number of women willing to collaborate and rise to the challenge – hopefully in more ways than one. As a first generation college student, I stumbled early in my career trying to navigate internal politics, while building a lasting network of peers, mentors, advisors and sponsors. Today, as a partner and a leader within PwC, I embrace those early experiences as motivation to learn, grow and act with intention when it comes to advancing diversity and inclusion. Over the past several years, I’ve worked with my local leadership and universities throughout the city of Chicago to establish the ‘PwC Honors’ program. This program engages area schools with large student bodies of racial and ethnic minorities to give their top students a glimpse into accounting before they officially start their careers. Since 2012, PwC has hosted hundreds of students from the University of Illinois at Chicago, DePaul University, Loyola University, Roosevelt University – and yes, my alma mater Robert Morris University. This is one way that I’m answering these questions and contributing to building a more diverse workforce. We as business leaders must individually have a commitment to, and accountability for, contributing to building diversity within our respective business areas. Research has shown that 85 percent of organizations agree that diversity results in the most innovative ideas and there are a myriad of benefits including smarter teams that have the potential to drive greater market growth. Bottom line: We already know that diversity is a competitive advantage and as businesses, we need to better reflect the communities where we reside and the clients that we serve. While we need to be asking ourselves the right questions, we as leaders and individuals also need to be accountable for answering them correctly and with action, nurturing diversity across our organizations.

Blake attended the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, where he received a Bachelor of Science in Accountancy in 2012, followed by a Masters of Accounting Science in 2013. He completed the CPA exam in 2013, and became a licensed CPA in 2014.  

Blake started at Deloitte St. Louis in 2013 and began working a wide variety of federal tax compliance engagements for partnerships, corporations, individuals, and trusts.  He started working on clients in Deloitte's Chicago office in 2015 to focus on tax work for the financial services industry, specializing in partnership tax compliance for family offices, hedge funds, and fund of funds. 

Blake joined PwC in 2016 as an experienced senior within Chicago's federal financial services tax department.  He was promoted to Manager in 2018 and provided tax services for a variety of hedge funds, private equity funds, and fund of funds. 

Blake joined the DFMC family office in 2019 as a manager in the entity accounting group.  

In 2022, Blake moved to St. Louis, MO and rejoined PwC's financial services tax department as a senior manager.

headline: Principal @ PwC • Cyber Remediation & Application Architecture Improvements for Financial Services Firms
about:
WHAT I DO: I partner with large financial services firms, generally in wealth management, to improve their application architecture and achieve their goals for Digital Transformation, IT Management, Cybersecurity, and Analytics.

HOW I DO IT: I am a digital director with PwC with eighteen years of IT consulting and executive leadership. Most of my work is cyber remediation for existing apps, but I also build new apps and environments for secure apps. 

WHO I WORK WITH: Executive and Managing Directors of IT/IT Security for large financial services companies.

WHY IT WORKS: As technology, client expectations, and security threats constantly evolve, my focus stays locked into creating solutions with three key features: they keep apps secure, improve client experience, and increase efficiency. I take a collaborative role with clients to help them understand the options that will address their issues and develop the vision of what they want to accomplish. Then I bring the resources together and manage projects to get them done on time and on budget. 

WHAT MAKES ME DIFFERENT: With a background in computer science and economics, and an MBA in accounting and finance, I develop IT strategy and solutions that are practical and cost effective. They’re not the fanciest options, but their simplicity means that they’ll get done. I’m also incorporating analytics, robotics, and other new technology to solve client problems, unlike some industry peers who are still building the same solutions as five years ago.

WANT TO TALK? Reach out to me here on LinkedIn.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Accounting Professor
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: July 31, 2025, David managed Jack directly
receivedRecommendations.description:
It is my pleasure to recommend Jack Blazevich.

I have known Jack from his time as a student at The University of Iowa. 

Jack took two courses I teach: Accounting Systems and Analytics (ACCT 3600) and Advanced Managerial Accounting (ACCT 4200). Jack did extremely well in both courses. 

More importantly, Jack was the President and Vice President of The University of Iowa’s Beta Alpha Psi chapter. I am our Chapter’s Faculty Advisor.

Beta Alpha Psi has high requirements for becoming a member; a high GPA, 10 volunteer hours, and 10 professional hours to be completed each semester.  Jack went above and beyond, even further than other members, by volunteering to be our Vice President and then President. Our Chapter President has a lot of responsibility, including planning and organizing all of our chapter’s events.

Jack’s crowning achievement as President was to plan, organize, and execute every detail of our annual Meet the Firms Night in September 2024.  We had a record attendance with 299 students and 38 employers.  Every year the University’s Career Center helps us with registration. The Career Center staff was very impressed with Jack’s leadership in running this event.

Over the last fifteen years, I have taught Accounting and Finance courses to over 6,800 students, at five different universities. I am also familiar with business careers outside of higher education. Before I entered higher education, I worked in industry for over twenty years. 

I know that Jack’s accomplishments while leading our Beta Alpha Psi chapter have given him valuable leadership experience that few business professionals his age have. 

I am more than confident that his leadership, work ethic, and positive energy will make significant contributions to any organization.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Professor of Practice of Accounting at University of Iowa
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: May 21, 2025, Kay was Jack’s teacher
receivedRecommendations.description:
I am honored to have had the opportunity to meet Jack as a student at the University of Iowa in the fall of 2024.  Prior to joining the Tippie accounting faculty, I practiced public accounting for 35 years.  As a personnel partner, I was responsible for recruiting, training, mentoring and retaining tax professionals.  I encountered only a handful of young professionals in the same league as Jack.  Jack is an individual blessed with many gifts.  Jack is a rare individual because of what he does with those gifts.  While his resume is impressive, even more impressive to me is Jack the man relative to his accomplishments.
Each student is required to visit me in my office the first week of class.  The goal of the meeting is for me to get to know him; I found him equally interested in getting to know me.  His bright, inquisitive eyes and huge smile drew me in.  The conversation was effortless.  He told me that while grades are important, he is more focused on what he can learn from each class, his mastery of the course content and what he can contribute during his time at the university.   I believed him then and I believed him even more at the end of the semester.  
Jack seeks opportunities to make a difference and expand his perspective of the world, not just for his own sake, but to help and empower others.  He generously shares his passion for learning and makes incredible investments of his time whether serving as a leader in Beta Alpha Psi or providing VITA services and tutoring to those who are not as blessed as he is.  Jack truly exemplifies the essence of what it means to be a leader, and he truly does this every single day.

Max is a Senior Manager in PwC's Advisory Workforce Transformation Consulting practice. His role involves driving transformation and change management, with a focus on improving the experience of frontline workers in major Consumer Markets companies. Max excels in driving sustainable change management by bridging culture, business value and technology capabilities. He is skilled in fostering cross-functional collaboration and linking the frontline workforce with the corporate center through technology-driven experiences. 

His primary work revolves around promoting sustainable, grassroots-led organizational change management, encompassing change readiness planning, strategic communication and training, stakeholder engagement and leadership alignment, and program management. 

Beyond his primary duties, Max aids clients in developing and implementing employee engagement strategies and platforms to enhance collaboration, connection, and retention among employees.  

Max, along with his husband, lives in the New York Metropolitan area.

headline: Director in PwC's Workforce Transformation Rewards & Wellbeing Practice
about:
Caroline is a Director in PwC's Workforce Transformation Rewards & Wellbeing practice specializing in Retirement. An actuary by background, Caroline has a passion for working with employers on holistic benefit plan and total rewards solutions. She enjoys teaming with HR, Tax and Finance on developing creative strategies for compensation and benefit programs, and brings the breadth of our Workforce Transformation and overall PwC teams' expertise to her clients.

Her experience includes tax efficient benefit plan strategy and wealth accumulation using qualified retirement plans, actuarial valuations, retirement plan administration, solutioning with employers to streamline benefit plan processes and improve participant experience, defined benefit/defined contribution plan design, governance and compliance, identifying and executing pension de-risking strategies, plan terminations, vendor search and selection, internal audit and governance consulting, merger and acquisition strategy, benefits utilization analysis, participant education and more. She also supports our audit practice as a specialist in reviewing pension and other postretirement benefit plan accounting aspects of our clients' corporate and plan financial statements. 

Caroline is an Associate of the Society of Actuaries and an Enrolled Actuary. She has a BS in Actuarial Mathematics from the University of Michigan.

A recent transplant from Chicago to Seattle, Caroline is loving the PNW - outside the PwC office, you can find her in the North Cascades learning to snowboard in the winter and hiking/camping/backpacking in the summer!

headline: International Tax Services - Quantitative Solutions & Technologies Senior Associate at PwC
about:
I am an ambitious, helpful analyzer who loves to teach as much as I love to learn, aspiring to professionally develop and collaborate with others to solve real-world problems using data and logic.

After determining solutions to problems, I like to share my knowledge with those around me as a mentor and as a peer. At the Kelley School of Business, I was a Teaching Assistant for a Technology and Business Analysis course for two years where I collaborated with hundreds of students in class and office hours to develop their capabilities using Microsoft Excel. I am currently a Graduate Teaching Assistant for a Financial Reporting and Analysis course, where I teach three discussion sections of about 30 students each. I hope to incorporate both learning and teaching into my long-term career.

I love to be challenged and collaborate in teams with colleagues who push me to grow. In high school, I was the CEO of a profitable company in an Entrepreneurship class. I also competed in an economics competition called the Fed Challenge, where my team and I presented to a panel of judges at the Federal Reserve in Chicago. In the 2018 Deloitte Data Challenge, I led a team to the case finals where we were presented with coffee shop data and asked to model potential outcomes for new initiatives and give recommendations. 

I have had this passion for analyzing and breaking problems down since elementary school. When I was in third grade, I came home after trick or treating and organized my Halloween candy. I then created a bar graph on Microsoft Excel to see which candies were the most popular that year. This sparked a lifelong passion of determining a problem, analyzing data, and discovering a solution using digital technologies. I am preparing to become a CPA, and I hope to pursue a career in Tax Accounting within a work environment that will foster collaboration and excellence.

headline: Director at PwC
about:
Over twenty-year actuarial consulting and risk management career helping Global Insurance companies manage risk, product portfolio and increase shareholder value. Worked with multi-disciplinary and cross-cultural teams spanning the globe.

Country experience covers North America (Canada, U.S), Latin America (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru, Uruguay),  Asia (Malaysia, Thailand), Europe (Spain, France, UK), Africa (South Africa).

Risk Decision and Management: Held role of Chief Risk Officer (CRO) in multiple countries. Executed de-risking of investment portfolio following financial crisis. Implemented ERM framework in ING Latin America regional office and advised countries on approach. 

Product Management: Developed wide range of life, non life and health products including those with participating features. Reviewed and approved product submissions in the role of Appointed Actuary. 

Business Transformation: Focused on rationalizing product portfolio, reducing reporting cycle and creating risk structure following separation of role of CFO and CRO. 

Leadership and People Development: Championed individual development, succession planning for key positions.

Business Development: Lead efforts for NMG’s expansion into South America and growth of Tillinghast-Towers Perrin business in Latin America.

Strategy Development and Execution: Developed strategies for growth through acquisition, market segmentation. Reviewed and supported business plan development. Constructed actuarial models on a variety of platforms including TAS, MoSes, Prophet, Axis to support business efforts.

experience.description:
Jorge is a director in PwC's Life Actuarial and Insurance Management Solutions. He supports US clients in their domestic and international operations (primarily Latin America). 

Our Actuarial & Insurance Management Solutions (AIMS) Practice is one of the largest actuarial consulting groups in the US, and consists of over 175 credentialed life/health and P&C actuaries located throughout the country. In addition to supporting PwC’s audits of 18 of the top 50 US life insurers, our life consulting team has 55 actuaries based in New York, Boston, Hartford, Philadelphia and Chicago. Our global AIMS network consists of over 1,000 professionals in 35 countries, which enables us to serve clients wherever they do business.

Jorge provides a range of actuarial, risk and capital management, transaction advisory services to PwC’s life insurance clients.

Jorge's Specialties: Actuarial and risk function transformation, Insurance Risk and Capital Management, Rationalization of Product portfolio, Insurance M&A, IFRS reporting and SII capital implementation.

Managed family investment portfolio
Consulted around strategy with SME's

headline: Experienced Assurance Associate at PwC | CPA Candidate
about:
I am Robert Strobel, a two-time graduate of Quinlan School of Business, Loyola University Chicago, with a strong foundation in accounting, information systems, and analytics. I earned my Bachelor of Business Administration in Accounting in December 2022 and completed my Master of Science in Information Systems and Analytics, along with a Business Data Analytics Certificate, in May 2024. Throughout my academic journey, I consistently excelled, making the Dean's List in 2020 and achieving Dean's Honors with a GPA higher than 3.9 during my graduate studies. Additionally, I have earned more than 150 credits, making me an eligible CPA candidate.

Born and raised in Chicago, my professional career began at O'Hare International Airport, where I worked as a Passenger Service Assistant and was quickly promoted to Lead Advisor. Following this, I consulted for Ryan Banks Academy as an External Consultant through Loyola and later worked as an International Tax Intern at ITW before embarking on my dream to continue my career in Miami.

Currently, I am an assurance associate at PwC in Miami, where I work across a variety of industries and focus on audit and assurance services. My educational background and professional experience allows me to effectively apply both technical and business insights to deliver high-quality services for clients. I am continually growing in my role, taking on new challenges, and expanding my knowledge.

I am a friendly and extroverted individual who enjoys meeting new people and building lasting relationships. My interests include continuous learning, traveling, exploring different cultures, and embracing new experiences. I love stepping out of my comfort zone and saying “yes” to activities that challenge me.

headline: Economist
about:
I have always been interested in economics and financial markets. This curiosity led me to do a Ph.D. in Economics to deepen my understanding of the tools economists use to model the world. To complement my skills with business knowledge, I completed an MBA at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business. I have focused my MBA on applied data analytics, financial topics, and strategy classes, which have allowed me to explore real-world business problems and solutions.

My work experience has always been centered around working on interesting economic issues. I have worked at public, private and academic sectors in a variety of positions, from economic research to teaching. Currently, I work at PwC as a Transfer Pricing Senior Associate, where I conduct industry analysis, perform valuations, and evaluate the debt capacity of multinational firms.  As a consultant, my job is to understand multiple industries and the underlying economics of each intercompany transaction. 

Keywords: economist, economics, research, finance, CFA, MBA, analytics, data analysis, data analytics.

publications.title: Negative Interest Rates: A Transfer Pricing Perspective
publications.description: The transfer pricing perspective regarding negative interest rates needs to consider the application of similar, uncontrolled, transaction pricing in its entirety (i.e., not just considering the stand-alone transactions but also the collateral transactions and policy environment). Given the activities of monetary policy makers, and subsequent market agent behavior, deviating from direct market observations may be warranted in an intercompany context under certain circumstances. We have provided examples of two common cash pool structures where allowing for negative interest rates may or may not be appropriate. Ultimately, each framework should be analyzed on a case-by-case basis with relevant applicable facts.

headline: Director - Deals at PwC
about:
Paul is a Director in PwC’s Deals practice in Los Angeles, California advising clients with complex accounting and financial reporting issues related to deals, including mergers & acquisitions, deal structures, capital market transactions, capital raising and other complex accounting issues. Paul began his career in the PwC Deals practice in the Chicago office. In February of 2014, Paul transferred to the Los Angeles office in order to help build and grow the practice.

He specializes in providing support with accounting and financial reporting issues associated with the SEC registration process, Initial Public Offerings , 144a debt and equity offerings, divestitures/carve-outs, and business combinations.  Paul has deep technical accounting and financial reporting knowledge across a variety topics including (but not limited to): accounting for business combinations, segment reporting/reporting units, the SEC registration process, pro forma financial statements, and private equity exit strategies. Paul has worked in a wide variety of industries including:  automotive, pharma and life sciences, entertainment and gaming, and technology.

Paul received his Bachelor of Science in Accountancy and Master of Accounting Science degrees from the College of Business at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. Paul is a Certified Public Accountant in California and Illinois and also a member of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

about:
Stella is a Partner at PwC with leadership responsibilities across market, solutions and service teams. With almost 15 years' experience at PwC, she has held various leadership roles, including leading service teams for many of PwC's largest clients, with a focus on the technology, media and telecommunications (TMT) and private equity (PE) sectors. 

Office Managing Partner: Stella is the Office Managing Partner for PwC's NY office. As the face of the firm to the local community and businesses, she is passionate about driving market-driven corporate responsibility initiatives and delivering value to clients. She believes in providing pragmatic solutions balanced with creative flexibility to save clients time and money. She is equally passionate about all aspects of firm-wide activities, including people, community and workplace management.

Deals and Private Equity: In her role as Cyber Risk and Reg's (CRR) Deals Solution Lead and PE CRR Platform Lead, Stella ensures that clients receive expert guidance and advice to maximise deal value and reduce transaction risk. By focusing on the technology and digital aspects of a transaction, Stella advances her clients' objectives as they undertake complex, global integrations, divestitures, separations and joint ventures. Her clients value approaches that accelerate risk identification and mitigation strategies to achieve desired deal synergies and increase shareholder value.

Transformation, XaaS, Analytics & Automation: Stella has also worked with clients undergoing complex business transformations, advising them on the cross-functional implications specifically related to their business processes, systems and controls. Stella has also led the analysis of data at scale, including big data analysis, data validation and visual analytics. She also leads system implementations, particularly for solutions that support revenue growth through subscription and consumption business models and the new leasing standard. 

In addition, Stella has extensive and broad assurance experience in areas such as SEC, technical accounting, financial and operational controls, internal audit and compliance. She is a national speaker at various forums. She is a Certified Public Accountant in NY and a Fellow of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. She is extremely passionate about making a difference in the community and serves on several non-profit boards and is a committed supporter of issues such as mental health, education and poverty/equality for all.

headline: ETS Senior Associate at PwC
about:
I am a 3rd year student at DePaul University, currently enrolled in the Driehaus School of Business. I am a hardworking, first-generation college student, looking for opportunities that will help me expand my technical and on-the-job knowledge. 

When I graduate, I will become the first person in my immediate family to obtain a college education. I did not know what I was going to study, when I first enrolled at DePaul University, so I initially wanted to pursue a career in Accounting. While accounting was pleasant, it did not spark my interest. It was time for a switch. After the two years I studied accounting, I began to study information systems; more particularly, the design, analysis, and management of them. I love the challenge of fitting the needs of not only the client, but designing systems to fully maximize the potential and efficiency of a specific business need. 

While my college/book education will help me gain a base understanding into some of the on-job activities, it is not until you begin working, till you understand what you will be doing. A base understanding is very important in most career paths, but having experience is what really provides a learning experience. Venturing into a career in anything related to IT/IS requires a lot of awareness, as technology is always changing. We always hear rumors about the next smartphone, days before the newest one is released. People are never satisfied. Similarly, in an ever-changing business environment, nothing is guaranteed, and a newer, sleeker system may provide a business a competitive edge. I was not certain where I would be two years ago, as a college freshman, but currently, I am sure of my educational pursuits, as well as my career aspirations.

projects.title: Data Analysis using Cloudera Hue on Microsoft Azure
projects.description: The project was a part of my course work titled Big Data using Hadoop. I used the data from California bike sharing system from the Bay Area to analyse various factors. My focus was more on the Cloud platform which in this case was Microsoft Azure. I used the virtual machine on Azure to run the Cloudera Enterprise Edition which had 1 Master node and 2 Slave nodes making it 3 total instances.  The system used 112 GB of memory for all the processing. Once the data was imported using the ETL tools, I used Hue to fire SQL-like queries for relevant data. Cloudera Enterprise Edition has built-in graphs tools which visualises the query results on the fly. More information can be found in the attached link for presentation.

projects.title: Sentiment Analysis of Twitter using Apache Storm
projects.description: As a team , we analysed the sentiments of Twitter users by fetching their tweets using an API in real time. The sentiments were categorized into positive, negative and neutral. The technology that we used is Apache Storm which is a distant cousin of Apache Hadoop.  It is a fault tolerant and real time technology. Before the actual implementation of the project we published a research paper explaining the overall gist of the project.

projects.title: Bike Management System using SQL and VB.NET

For instance, the customer can view all the bikes which are up for sale by the company. It was basically an eshowroom with the pictures and specifications of the bike. If there was an existing user, he can login using his credentials for servicing his bike. There was a job card which listed all the services which are needed. An estimate bill was generated with the addition of the cost of all the services.

about:
I’m a Director in PwC’s Capital Markets and Accounting Advisory Services practice, where I advise companies on the financial reporting complexities that arise throughout the deal lifecycle — from IPO readiness and cross-border listings to mergers, carve-outs, and complex technical accounting matters.

With a core focus on supporting CFOs and deal teams, I help clients navigate technical accounting, SEC compliance, and capital markets execution with clarity, precision, and confidence. I specialize in advising clients across the Technology, Media & Telecommunications (TMT) and Consumer Products sectors, bringing a nuanced understanding of industry-specific challenges and evolving regulatory standards.

I recently returned to the U.S. following a two-year secondment with PwC UK’s Deals Advisory practice in London, where I advised on multinational transactions involving dual listings across the U.S., U.K., and Netherlands.

- Capital markets transactions (IPO readiness, S-1/F-1 filings, dual-listings)

publications.title: Military Lending Act (MLA): It's time to get prepared
publications.description:
Protecting the financial interests of servicemembers and their families is a spotlight issue for both the prudential regulatory agencies and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB). In 2011, the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (DFA) established the Office of Servicemember Affairs (OSA) within the CFPB for the purpose of developing and implementing initiatives to educate and empower servicemembers to make better informed decisions regarding financial products and services. 

Since then, a number of supervisory and enforcement actions have been taken against lenders for violations of consumer financial protection laws and regulations that caused harm to servicemembers, including harm arising from violations of the Servicemembers’ Civil Relief Act (SCRA). 

In a continuation of the theme of protecting servicemembers from financial harm, on July 21, 2015 the Department of Defense (DoD) issued the final rule amending the regulations implementing the Military Lending Act (MLA). 

Read this publication to learn more about the expanded scope of covered products under the final rule and how your business may be impacted.

headline: Assurance Associate @ PwC
about:
I am a graduate of The George Washington University School of Business Master’s of Accountancy graduate program. Before that, I received two Bachelor's of Science Degrees in Accountancy and Finance from GW’s undergraduate program. I recently passed all four of the CPA Exams, and I am currently finishing my remaining requirements to achieve certification.

During my time in college, I interned with Johnson Lambert, Plante Moran, and PwC. At Johnson Lambert, I worked as an Audit Intern in their Virginia office. There, I worked on audit engagements for insurance and not-for-profit organizations which allowed me to develop proficient knowledge of the audit process. At Plante Moran, I worked as an Assurance Intern in their Schaumburg office. There, I worked on employee benefit plans and off year-end audits for companies in the healthcare and manufacturing industries. This allowed me to further develop my knowledge of the audit process while also exposing me to different accounting practices and standards. At PwC, I was an Assurance Intern in their Asset and Wealth Management division where we worked on year-end funds. These experiences honed my skills in auditing, compliance, and financial reporting, providing a strong foundation in the field of assurance services. I am currently working full-time with PwC as an Assurance Associate in their Chicago office.

My interests include playing sports such as golf and basketball, traveling and fitness.

headline: Learning Experience & Technology Leader
about:
I’m a relentless advocate for the learner experience! Whether internal or external, the learner is our customer and we need to know them, their wants and needs, and how well our products serve them to keep them coming back.

I’m a genuine, empathetic leader with a reputation for building great teams.

I’ve been told I have a contagious passion for the work I do—we do cool stuff…why wouldn’t I be excited about it, all the time?

I am a voracious learner, with a passion for emerging technology.

I’m an adept consultant and analyst—I love getting in the weeds, balancing competing inputs and priorities, and synthesizing a “big picture” strategy.

I’m a successful leader of virtual, cross-functional teams who design, develop, and deliver cutting-edge learning solutions that drive performance, engagement, and business results.

experience.position: Sr. Manager, Learning, Innovation, and Technology
experience.description:
-Provide strategic oversight for a blended portfolio consisting of proprietary custom-developed solutions, third part SaaS products, and associated cross-platform integrations. 
-Lead product strategy, product development, and associated release management for core proprietary Learning & Development platforms within the PwC US ecosystem. 
-Design, conduct, and analyze voice-of-the-customer sessions to capture stories for our product roadmaps, drive adoption, and elevate associated onboarding design. 
-Lead an agile, cross-functional, global team of business analysts, engineers, and QA resources to execute our business goals, roadmap items, production support, establish trust and a deeper partnership with key business partners.

As the Sr. Manager of Learning Experience & Technology at Fifth Third Bank, I lead a team that is responsible for the Learning Experience & supporting technology/digital learning strategies at the Bank—Learner Experience, Industry Research & Best Practices, Marketing & Adoption, Data Analysis & Visualization, and the Learning Technology Ecosystem.

I set the strategic vision and direction for learning experiences at Fifth Third Bank, through industry and vendor research, employee insights, analysis and synthesis--all in service of storytelling and driving innovation. topSkills: Agile Project Management • Customer Success • Go-to-Market Strategy • Customer Segmentation Strategy • Customer Lifecycle Management
about:
Delivering exceptional customer experiences has been at the heart of my career for over 8 years. At PwC, my role as a Product Activation & Customer Success Manager centers on maximizing customer value through strategy and innovation in AI transformation products. Creating go-to-market plans with a foundation in Agile methodologies and an array of tools like Gainsight, Pendo and Sprinklr my focus is on accelerating digital delivery that aligns with client goals and enables upsell, cross-sell and renewals. Creating go-to-mat commitment to customer satisfaction is evidenced by our meticulously tracked metrics, such as time to value and NPS.

The hands-on experience from my previous role at Morningstar has honed my skills in customer segmentation and lifecycle marketing, directly contributing to enhanced acquisition, adoption and retention. Collaboratively leading cross-functional teams, I've developed and implemented playbooks and processes that not only meet but exceed stakeholder expectations. This has established me as a trusted advisor who enables clients to thrive in an increasingly digital landscape.

experience.description: As Product Activation & Customer Success Manager for workforce transformation SaaS products, I manage enterprise customer accounts with a focus on retention, adoption, and growth, building playbooks and processes to enhance customer satisfaction by tracking time to value and NPS. Leveraging Agile methodologies, I accelerate the delivery of high-quality digital services, improving the client experience. I develop trusted advisor relationships with key stakeholders, ensuring success plans aligned with their business goals, while facilitating technical and strategic workshops to drive consensus and actionable outcomes. Through multiple client touch points and using tools such as Gainsight, Pendo and SFDC, I identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities, collaborate with internal teams to enhance customer value, and track key milestones to provide executive-level insights.

In my role as a Product Marketing Manager, I owned the strategy and execution of lifecycle marketing, creating initiatives for each stage of the customer journey. By leveraging user behavior, activity data, research, and industry-specific insights, I developed customer segmentation and personalization strategies for email campaigns. I partnered with analytics, product, and marketing teams to optimize channels and drive retention, while building hypothesis-based tests to refine segmentation, channel, and messaging for key results.

As a member of the Bosch Auto Service team, I led initiatives to transition the automotive aftermarket industry into the digital realm. By crafting and executing lead generation and digital analytics strategies, I enhanced operational efficiency and streamlined the partner experience within the program. headline: Data Risk & Privacy Director - PwC
about:
Katy ​(CIPP/US, CIPP/E) is a Director with PwC’s Data Risk & Privacy group, working with global and domestic clients to understand and improve their current capability to comply with various regulations as part of a holistic data privacy and security strategy. Katy has diverse legal and data protection experience including regulatory compliance, policy management, information security, third party management, and training. 

Katy leads breach analytics and notification projects, supporting the definition, identification, and quantification of sensitive data for the purpose of notifying individuals, business partners, and regulators. Katy leads PwC's Privacy Deals team, providing data privacy expertise in M&A due diligence and pre/post close support and IPO readiness, complimenting the Cyber Deals services. Katy also focuses on healthcare privacy and risk management, supporting  traditional health and pharma organizations and healthcare adjacent companies address new privacy and digital health challenges. She manages global and domestic projects, executing assessments, defining strategy, and implementing program processes and tech aligned to GDPR, US State Privacy laws, HIPAA, NIST, and ISO requirements. Her experience provides clients with an understanding of what is required for a defensible privacy compliance program and how to achieve it.

Prior to joining PwC, Katy worked in healthcare compliance and practiced law, including commercial litigation and transactional health law. She has a Juris Doctorate and Health Law Certificate from Loyola University Chicago School of Law (Chicago, IL) and a Bachelors in Sociology from University the of Kansas (Lawrence, KS).

about:
I currently lead the Assurance practice for PwC’s MidCentral Region. As a member of the firm’s extended leadership team, I am driven to uphold PwC’s purpose: to build trust in society and solve important problems. With over 30 years of industry experience, I have served a variety of clients in the consumer, industrial products and life sciences industries. I have served as the engagement partner on numerous multinational companies, with ultimate responsibility for delivering client service and audit quality. In my roles as both partner and regional leader, I not only oversee the quality of our assurance services, but also focus on developing our team of over 4000 people while driving innovation and efficiency.

receivedRecommendations.description:
Disciplined and dedicated – good qualities to have as an Accountant! David Garcia can count these among his strengths.  I met David in the Fall of 2021 when he enrolled in my BA 420 Professional Presence class at UIC. He was early for every class, always prepared, and scored an impressive 99.23% on his homework assignments.

We worked on articulating life experiences, career exploration, interviewing skills, improvisation, networking, and public speaking. David had two goals coming into this class: 1) get an internship and 2) get more comfortable with public speaking. He nailed both!

He worked on his resume, revamped his LinkedIn profile, wrote stories that demonstrated critical competencies illustrated through his life experiences, practiced responding to common interview questions, interviewed several accountants, joined the Accounting Club, attended the Accounting Career Fair, and scored a busy-season tax internship – goal #1 achieved!

Between the many improv games we played and the numerous impromptu speeches on random topics, David increased his confidence and ability to think on his feet. His midterm and final presentations proved that he is both an effective presenter and an excellent public speaker. Goal #2 accomplished!

David is clear on his goals and his career path. I am confidant that he will be a Partner in a top-tier public accounting firm in the not-too-distant future. He carries my highest recommendation!

projects.associatedWith: Associated with Price Waterhouse Management Consultants
projects.description: Researching, interviewing, and writing an article about urbanism and aging demographics in a global context.  Against a backdrop of demographic mega-trends--low fertility rates combined with looming elder population projections--many have suggested that an unsustainable economic crisis is on the horizon. This article acknowledges the seriousness of the demographic trends but finds many options that suggest a manageable path. Cities themselves are part of the solution, and the article looks at three cities in particular that are facing aging demographics head on--Tokyo, Seoul, and Stockholm.

The article appears in sixth issue of Cities of Opportunity.

about:
Julie is a Partner at PwC with leadership responsibilities across market, solutions and service teams. With almost 20 years' experience at PwC, she has held various leadership roles, including leading service teams for many of PwC's largest clients, with a focus on the technology, media and telecommunications (TMT) and private equity (PE) sectors. 

Office Managing Partner: Julie is the Office Managing Partner for PwC's NY office. As the face of the firm to the local community and businesses, she is passionate about driving market-driven corporate responsibility initiatives and delivering value to clients. She believes in providing pragmatic solutions balanced with creative flexibility to save clients time and money. She is equally passionate about all aspects of firm-wide activities, including people, community and workplace management.

Deals and Private Equity: In her role as Cyber Risk and Reg's (CRR) Deals Solution Lead and PE CRR Platform Lead, Julie ensures that clients receive expert guidance and advice to maximise deal value and reduce transaction risk. By focusing on the technology and digital aspects of a transaction, Julie advances her clients' objectives as they undertake complex, global integrations, divestitures, separations and joint ventures. Her clients value approaches that accelerate risk identification and mitigation strategies to achieve desired deal synergies and increase shareholder value.

Transformation, XaaS, Analytics & Automation: Julie has also worked with clients undergoing complex business transformations, advising them on the cross-functional implications specifically related to their business processes, systems and controls. Julie has also led the analysis of data at scale, including big data analysis, data validation and visual analytics. She also leads system implementations, particularly for solutions that support revenue growth through subscription and consumption business models and the new leasing standard. 

In addition, Julie has extensive and broad assurance experience in areas such as SEC, technical accounting, financial and operational controls, internal audit and compliance. She is a national speaker at various forums. She is a Certified Public Accountant in NY and a Fellow of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. She is extremely passionate about making a difference in the community and serves on several non-profit boards and is a committed supporter of issues such as mental health, education and poverty/equality for all.

As a recent MBA graduate from the University of Miami’s Herbert School of Business, I bring a diverse academic and professional background spanning international relations, economics, media production, and business strategy. My international education and 7 years of experience in the U.S. have equipped me with a global mindset and cross-functional expertise. Now, I am eager to leverage my multidisciplinary knowledge to drive impactful solutions in the business world, aligning my career with my passion for strategic problem-solving and value creation.

After returning to China, I began my professional journey at ​PwC Shanghai​, joining the ​Asset & Wealth Management (AWM) Research Team​ in June 2023. Over 1.5 years, I contributed to ​research, consulting, and audit support​, helping clients navigate complex financial landscapes. In October 2024, I transitioned to the ​Risk Assurance – GRC (Governance, Risk & Compliance) team​, where I now focus on ​risk management, internal audit, compliance, and corporate governance​.

At PwC, I am committed to solving critical business challenges and fostering ​trust in society​—whether through robust risk frameworks, strategic insights, or governance excellence. publications.title: Evolving healthcare provider ERM programs
publications.description: PwC conducted research to assess the state of enterprise risk management (ERM) within healthcare providers and found many are operating at comparable levels to their peers. However, given the increasingly complex and risk saturated environment providers operate in, there’s an urgency for providers to continuously enhance and improve their ERM programs beyond their current capabilities.

publications.title: Integrating enterprise risk management and business continuity management
publications.description: Organizations that integrate enterprise risk management (ERM) into their strategic planning efforts have found that business continuity management (BCM) enhances both their value creation objectives and their protection objectives. The confidence that comes from identifying and appropriately addressing interruption risks enables them to more boldly execute those strategic plans. But to gain that confidence requires the melding of ERM and BCM programs.

publications.title: Integration opportunities for ERM programs
publications.description: The best way to sustain enterprise risk management (ERM) programs—and generate ongoing value–is to integrate risk management processes with other business activities. Successful integration efforts require substantial planning and organization buy-in. We believe a comprehensive risk-management-process integration plan can improve risk management information, overall risk culture, and strategic decision making.

publications.title: Steps to Devising a Successful Enterprise Risk Management Program
publications.description: Quoted from my presentation at RIMS ERM Conference in Chicago, October 26th - 27th, 2015   “We see over and over where organizations start out really strong and have executive support, but then they don’t continue to steadily grow the risk management process at their organizations,” said Steve Zawoyski, Minneapolis-based partner and enterprise risk management leader at PwC.

publications.title: Integrating risk scenario analysis into an ERM program
publications.description: This publication describes the potential benefits from risk scenario analysis, and describes a methodology for introducing risk scenario analysis to support strategic decision-making.

publications.title: The evolution of ERM programs
publications.description: A primary goal of enterprise risk management (ERM) programs should be to create a sustainable and value-adding ERM program that can survive management turnover, shifting priorities, and resource challenges. This article describes common risk management program trajectories, common pitfalls, and a methodology and long-term plan for supporting a successful and relevant ERM program.

publications.title: Building a strategic ERM program
publications.description: Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) programs that focus on and are consistently aligned with the company’s strategic priorities are likely to provide the greatest benefits to organizations. This article articulates the challenges and provides real examples of how companies have aligned strategies with risk management activities.

publications.title: Why risk assessments fail
publications.description: Risk assessments are a foundational component of risk management programs, but often fail to fully support both program and business objectives. This article identifies the primary reasons for risk assessment fatigue and failure, and ways to improve success.

publications.title: Strategic risk management includes opportunities, not just risk
publications.description: Quoted - "As you go down that maturity, ultimately the goal is you want to include risk in your decision-making process, improving the way you make decisions and the speed at which you can make decisions,” said Steve Zawoyski, a partner at PricewaterhouseCoopers L.L.P. in Minneapolis.

publications.title: From Compliance to ERM
publications.description:
Regulators clearly want corporate boards to embrace the idea of enterprise risk management, and boards are leaning on compliance officers to start that process. This panel will explore how compliance officers can lead that charge, expanding beyond straightforward (if maddening) regulatory compliance to a more forward-looking approach to risk generally.
Featuring:
Peter Agnoletto, Chief Audit Executive and ERM Leader/Senior Director of Internal Audit, Par Pharmaceutical Companies

headline: Partner, Markets Leader, PricewaterhouseCoopers | Leader, Cyber Risk & Regulatory Private Equity & Transactions, PricewaterhouseCoopers | Member of the Board of Directors
about:
Vanessa is a Partner at PwC with leadership responsibilities across market, solutions and service teams. With almost 15 years' experience at PwC, she has held various leadership roles, including leading service teams for many of PwC's largest clients, with a focus on the technology, media and telecommunications (TMT) and private equity (PE) sectors. 

Office Managing Partner: Vanessa is the Office Managing Partner for PwC's NY office. As the face of the firm to the local community and businesses, she is passionate about driving market-driven corporate responsibility initiatives and delivering value to clients. She believes in providing pragmatic solutions balanced with creative flexibility to save clients time and money. She is equally passionate about all aspects of firm-wide activities, including people, community and workplace management.

Deals and Private Equity: In her role as Cyber Risk and Reg's (CRR) Deals Solution Lead and PE CRR Platform Lead, Vanessa ensures that clients receive expert guidance and advice to maximise deal value and reduce transaction risk. By focusing on the technology and digital aspects of a transaction, Vanessa advances her clients' objectives as they undertake complex, global integrations, divestitures, separations and joint ventures. Her clients value approaches that accelerate risk identification and mitigation strategies to achieve desired deal synergies and increase shareholder value.

Transformation, XaaS, Analytics & Automation: Vanessa has also worked with clients undergoing complex business transformations, advising them on the cross-functional implications specifically related to their business processes, systems and controls. Vanessa has also led the analysis of data at scale, including big data analysis, data validation and visual analytics. She also leads system implementations, particularly for solutions that support revenue growth through subscription and consumption business models and the new leasing standard. 

In addition, Vanessa has extensive and broad assurance experience in areas such as SEC, technical accounting, financial and operational controls, internal audit and compliance. She is a national speaker at various forums. She is a Certified Public Accountant in NY and a Fellow of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. She is extremely passionate about making a difference in the community and serves on several non-profit boards and is a committed supporter of issues such as mental health, education and poverty/equality for all.

headline: Global Structuring-Transfer Pricing Manager, PwC | Board Member | Economic Policy and Development Advocate
about:
I have a diverse experience working on a wide portfolio of projects including value chain transformation, transfer pricing planning, global structuring, and intangible property valuations, in addition to transfer pricing compliance and country-by-country reporting under both the US and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) frameworks. Served multinational companies operating in various jurisdictions around the world and across multiple industries including energy, petrochemicals, pharmaceutical, technology, consumer goods, and nonprofit. 

Prior to joining PwC, I have had the chance to lead the growth of a small local office to one of the highest-profile operation centers in the region. I devised creative strategies and business operations that created sustainable value and provided solutions to challenges that stunted the development of new businesses in the region and particularly hindered small manufacturers and startups. 

Other than transfer pricing and strategic management, I am passionate about language learning and international development. I currently speak three languages (Arabic, French, and English) and I am learning three more. I led and engaged in different initiatives focused on economic policy, systems change, and capacity building around the world. I was elected as one of the Women’s International League for Peace and Freedom (WILPF) US delegates to discuss challenges and opportunities for the empowerment of rural women at the Commission on the Status of Women review meetings at the United Nations Headquarters in New York, and participated in different discussions and summits held in collaboration with the United Nations Development Program (UNDP) and World Centre for Sustainable Development among others.

about:
Emily is a Partner at PwC with leadership responsibilities across market, solutions and service teams. With almost 15 years' experience at PwC, she has held various leadership roles, including leading service teams for many of PwC's largest clients, with a focus on the technology, media and telecommunications (TMT) and private equity (PE) sectors. 

Office Managing Partner: Emily is the Office Managing Partner for PwC's NY office. As the face of the firm to the local community and businesses, she is passionate about driving market-driven corporate responsibility initiatives and delivering value to clients. She believes in providing pragmatic solutions balanced with creative flexibility to save clients time and money. She is equally passionate about all aspects of firm-wide activities, including people, community and workplace management.

Deals and Private Equity: In her role as Cyber Risk and Reg's (CRR) Deals Solution Lead and PE CRR Platform Lead, Emily ensures that clients receive expert guidance and advice to maximise deal value and reduce transaction risk. By focusing on the technology and digital aspects of a transaction, Emily advances her clients' objectives as they undertake complex, global integrations, divestitures, separations and joint ventures. Her clients value approaches that accelerate risk identification and mitigation strategies to achieve desired deal synergies and increase shareholder value.

Transformation, XaaS, Analytics & Automation: Emily has also worked with clients undergoing complex business transformations, advising them on the cross-functional implications specifically related to their business processes, systems and controls. Emily has also led the analysis of data at scale, including big data analysis, data validation and visual analytics. She also leads system implementations, particularly for solutions that support revenue growth through subscription and consumption business models and the new leasing standard. 

In addition, Emily has extensive and broad assurance experience in areas such as SEC, technical accounting, financial and operational controls, internal audit and compliance. She is a national speaker at various forums. She is a Certified Public Accountant in NY and a Fellow of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. She is extremely passionate about making a difference in the community and serves on several non-profit boards and is a committed supporter of issues such as mental health, education and poverty/equality for all.

She believes in providing pragmatic solutions balanced with creative flexibility to save clients time and money. She is equally passionate about all aspects of firm-wide activities, including people, community and workplace management.

Deals and Private Equity: In her role as Cyber Risk and Reg's (CRR) Deals Solution Lead and PE CRR Platform Lead, Diana ensures that clients receive expert guidance and advice to maximise deal value and reduce transaction risk. By focusing on the technology and digital aspects of a transaction, Diana advances her clients' objectives as they undertake complex, global integrations, divestitures, separations and joint ventures. Her clients value approaches that accelerate risk identification and mitigation strategies to achieve desired deal synergies and increase shareholder value.

Transformation, XaaS, Analytics & Automation: Diana has also worked with clients undergoing complex business transformations, advising them on the cross-functional implications specifically related to their business processes, systems and controls. Diana has also led the analysis of data at scale, including big data analysis, data validation and visual analytics. about:
Joe Wiggins is an trust solutions assurance partner with PwC. He has over 30 years of experience specializing in financial services, and currently serves as the Global Alternative Funds Practice Leader for PwC. Prior to moving to Chicago in 2010, Joe spent most of his career working in the firm’s New York Asset and Wealth Management Practice.  Joe returned to New York in October 2021 to become one of the US Asset and Wealth Management team practice leaders.  He has extensive experience in investment fund audits with a particular focus on annual financial statement audits for non-registered and registered investment products, including private equity, hedge funds and investment companies. 

Joe has served many multi-billion dollar hedge fund firms with strategies including credit derivatives, macro, relative value and RMBS as well as currently serving several firms in the Chicago marketplace. In the private equity area, Joe's clients have included a major financial institution with more than 70 private equity funds and in excess of $6 billion of invested capital in middle-market buyouts, as well as growth equity and venture capital in the United States, Europe and Asia. Joe has also been one of the audit partners serving one of the world's leading private investment firms with approximately $25 billion under management in funds and accounts. Additionally, Joe was the engagement partner for a large 100+ registered investment fund complex of a major insurance company. 

Joe led the National Learning and Education program for the U.S. Asset and Wealth Management practice from 2003 to 2010. He is a frequent presenter at industry events, as well as PwC sponsored conferences. He served as a Board member of the Midwest Chapter of Hedge Fund Cares charity organization from 2010 to 2021 and a Board member and Treasurer for the Managed Funds Association from 2018-2021 and was an active partner champion of PwC's diversity, equality and inclusion efforts through the PwC Diversity Council for Chicago. Joe earned a Bachelor of Business Administration in accounting at the University of Iowa, and is a member of several CPA state societies as well as the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

projects.title: Crisis Communications Plan (severe snowfall at the Chicago Department of Streets and Sanitation)
projects.description:
An assignment for my Crisis Communications class during my senior year at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. We were assigned a company or organization — mine was the City of Chicago's Department of Streets and Sanitation — and had to come up with a plan in the event of a plausible crisis.
I focused my project on the crisis of "severe snowfall." I had to research the leaders of the department, as well as local news outlets and local emergency personnel that we would need to communicate with in the event of the crisis. I also gathered information on the city's snow/ice removal process and services and other tools (such as apps or notification systems) that may be of service to residents of Chicago in the event of the crisis.
As the "Crisis Communications Manager" I also created a fill-in-the-blanks news release to be used in the event of an "extreme snowfall incident" and created a list of "key messages" to share with employees so everyone is on the same page when talking to residents and/or the press.

She is Fellow of the Regional Studies Association (FeRSA), since 2022, as well as invited professor in the University of Santiago de Chile (since 2019) and University Rey Juan Carlos University, Madrid (since 2016). She was also visiting scholar in the University of Chicago (2017, 2018), Adolfo Ibáñez University, Chile (2014) and University of Illinois (2004), and visiting professor of the University of Franche-Comté, France (2013-2014). She is member of the editorial board of several journals like Journal of Geographical Systems. She was co-editor of the Journal Spatial Economic Analysis (2020-2023), among others. She directs the ECONRES research group and works in spatial econometrics and spatial statistics with applications to regional inequalities, housing prices, environment, tourism and quality of life. She is highly experienced in the generation of statistics on micro-territorial variables.

projects.title: Specification Searches in Spatial Econometric Models. Method and Practice (3SEM)
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Universidad Autónoma de Madrid
projects.description:
This project builds on the two main features of spatial econometrics, interdependence and heterogeneity, to which we add instability. We focus on the topics of uncertainty in the weights matrix and on the problem of changing regimes. Our framework are panel or pseudo-panel data models. In essence, this a methodological project with a strong applied research program. The weight matrix is a key element in the construction of an spatial model. Its specification follows from an a priori decision. This situation has begun to change in recent years, with more formal procedures. Our contribution sets out two lines of research. In first place, we want to elaborate an strategy to select the optimal weight matrix from among a finite group of matrices. Then we develop methods to detect when, using panel information, a change in the weights matrix has occurred. This result is necessary to tackle a more ambitious objective, the modeling of the weights matrix which should be estimated from the data. Regime changes mirror the instability of spatial relationships. In the past we have worked in that problem trying to detect breaks; our interest now is on modeling the breaks using two approaches: a discrete procedure based on Stat-Scan and a continuous one using STAR models. The first will be useful to differentiate between spatial dependence and groupwise heteroskedasticity, and also among different types of spatial dependence. STAR models have been recently introduced in a spatial context and our objective is to extend their use also to the mechanisms of spatial dependence. The purpose is to get rid of the restriction of symmetry, introducing higher nonlinearities in this kind of models.

Government of Spain for the project entitled "Specification Searches in Spatial Econometric Models. Method and Practice (3SEM)” (ref.: ECO2015-65758-P). Principal Investigator: Jesús Mur and Ana Angulo (University of Zaragoza, Spain).

projects.title: Atlas Socieconómico de Extremadura 2017
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Universidad Autónoma de Madrid
projects.description:
Con este IV Atlas Socioeconómico de Extremadura se consolida una publicación a todas luces necesaria para conocer con el mayor detalle posible cada uno de los 388 pueblos y ciudades de la región. Se trata de un compendio minucioso que suministra información muy diversa y valiosa que permite, sin duda, extraer conclusiones sobre los potenciales escenarios de desarrollo y de futuro de nuestra tierra.
Esta nueva edición incorpora, además de la actualización temporal de las series de datos ya presentadas en ocasiones anteriores, información de la deuda municipal, indice de actividad empresarial, análisis migratorio de Extremadura, tiempo de viaje a la cabecera de área e indicadores de emprendimiento sectorial.
El Atlas comprende nueve capítulos claramente diferenciados y que se refieren a Indicadores Económicos, Demográficos y Sociales; Áreas Comerciales; Indicadores de Emprendimiento; Evolución de Indicadores Estadísticos; Caracterización Sociodemográfica por distritos de los municipios más importantes; Indicadores Básicos de las Mancomunidades de Extremadura y Anexo de mapas temáticos. Se trata, por tanto, de un trabajo exhaustivo que año tras año va ganando en riqueza y en interés y que incluye estadísticas que se colocan, cada vez más, en el epicentro de los debates sociales y políticos.

It is the aim of both institutions to promote advanced research and learning between UAM and Latin-American universities in order to create and/or strengthen institutional networks. projects.title: Urban Audit
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Universidad Autónoma de Madrid
projects.description:
National figures alone cannot reveal the full and sometimes complex picture of what is happening at a more detailed level within the European Union (EU). In this respect, statistical information at a subnational level is an important tool for highlighting specific regional and territorial aspects. It helps in analysing changing patterns and the impact that policy decisions can have on our daily life. In order to provide a detailed picture of the diverse EU territories and to monitor EU regional policy targets, Eurostat has developed a range of statistics based on different classifications and typologies. These include data for: regions, cities and greater cities, metropolitan regions, rural areas and regions.
Specific geographies such as coastal regions, mountain regions, border regions or island regions are also covered.
